args.doc: Bullets in one pull. Default 1. A shotgunner is 3.
args.name: count

args.doc: Degrees of random cone, per bullet.
args.name: spread

args.doc: Tracer style to draw, or absent for none.
args.name: tracer

actions.doc: An instant shot. The engine answers where the ray ended and what was there; what that COSTS is this action.
actions.name: hitscan

args.doc: Degrees between shots when `count` > 1. A mancubus volley.
args.name: arc

args.doc: How far in front of the body it appears. Launched clear or it is touching its owner on the tick it exists.
args.name: offset

actions.doc: Launch one of the `missiles` defined in the same file.
actions.name: missile

actions.doc: Hurt the current target, with no range test. For a missile's `on_hit`, where contact has ALREADY been established by the flight -- `melee` measures from the actor, and a missile's actor is the mob that fired it, which by then is somewhere else entirely. That was a real bug: a fireball burst on the player and did nothing, because the range was being tested from twelve units back where the imp was standing.
actions.name: damage

actions.doc: Damage if the target is inside `range` right now. Separate from `hitscan` because a monster with only a ranged attack is harmless the moment you stand inside it -- a missile spawned inside somebody bursts on its owner or sails past.
actions.name: melee

actions.doc: A shove, in world units per second. A lost soul's charge, a leap.
actions.name: impulse

args.doc: Refuse if this many of that kind are already alive and owned by this one. A pain elemental without a budget fills the entity table.
args.name: limit

args.doc: Only this kind. Absent means any.
args.name: mob

actions.doc: Put a corpse in reach back on its feet. Costs no engine support: corpses are already a script-side list.
actions.name: revive

actions.doc: A blast. `hurts_owner` false is a rocket that does not kill the cyberdemon that fired it.
actions.name: damage_area

actions.doc: Writes tick + ticks into the var, for `cooldown_ready` to read.
actions.name: set_cooldown

actions.doc: Leave now, mid-sequence. The rest of the sequence does not run.
actions.name: goto

args.doc: Degrees, an ABSOLUTE world heading, for `towards = angle`. 0 is +x and it counts anticlockwise, which is what dnp.atan2 answers in.
args.name: angle

args.doc: A per-mob variable holding a heading, for `towards = var`. Written by `set_angle`, which is how a mob turns to something it worked out earlier.
args.name: var

args.doc: Degrees added after, signed. `towards = target` with an offset of 90 is a monster sidling across your front rather than walking into it.
args.name: offset

args.doc: Degrees of random slop either side, added last. Draws once, off the world's own stream, exactly as `chance` does -- so it replays.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc: Turn to face, once, at this instant. Doom's A_FaceTarget, and the reason a monster's shot goes where you are rather than where you were when it started winding up.
actions.name: face

args.doc: Degrees, for `towards = angle`.
args.name: angle

args.doc: Degrees of random slop either side.
args.name: jitter

actions.doc:
Work out a heading and keep it in a variable, for `face` and for `move = "wander"` to read.
AN ANGLE IS A NUMBER, so it lives in the same per-mob variables everything else does rather than in a second kind of storage: a turn is 2^32 and that is exact in a double, which is why brad are plain Lua numbers here and `homing` on a missile is an int.
`towards = random` is the one that makes wandering wander. Without it `move = "wander"` reads a heading nothing ever wrote and walks straight at the aim -- which it did, silently, for as long as the mode has existed.
actions.name: set_angle

actions.doc: A replicated movement parameter, by the name in core/include/dnp/physics/params_table.hpp. This is how a mob changes its own speed -- and because the parameter replicates, every client agrees without this file knowing the wire exists.
actions.name: set_param

actions.doc: A temporary modifier through the effect stack, which recomputes from base every tick and so cannot drift.
actions.name: effect

args.doc: Default 'player', which is what the runtime does on its own.
args.name: of

args.doc: How far to look. Absent means the mob's own `sight`.
args.name: distance

args.doc: Only this kind, when looking for a mob.
args.name: mob

args.doc: Only this record, when looking for a prop.
args.name: prop

args.doc: Require a clear ray. Costs one per candidate, so put a `distance` on it.
args.name: visible

actions.doc: Point this mob at the nearest thing that matches, or at nothing if none does.
actions.name: target_nearest

actions.doc: Turn on whatever last hurt it. The mob-level `infighting` field does this automatically and unconditionally; this is how a graph decides for itself -- retaliate only below half health, or only when the attacker is closer than what it is already chasing.
actions.name: target_attacker

actions.doc: Forget the current target. `has_target` is then false and the runtime will acquire again on a later think.
actions.name: target_none

actions.doc: The escape hatch. `mob` is in scope, and so is everything in dnp.*. Anything this vocabulary cannot say goes here, and that is what it is for -- a framework whose only extension point is adding to the framework is one nobody can build on.
actions.name: lua

conditions.doc: Something is being hunted at all.
conditions.name: has_target

conditions.doc: Plan distance, not 3D: a cacodemon above you is still near you.
conditions.name: target_within

conditions.doc: A ray reaches it. NOT the same question as `target_within`, and conflating them is what had monsters shooting through two walls at somebody across the map. Costs a raycast -- put a `target_within` before it.
conditions.name: target_visible

args.doc: Degrees either side of facing. Default 90.
args.name: arc

conditions.doc: Whether the target is within the arc the mob is facing.
conditions.name: target_in_front

conditions.doc: How long it has been in the current state.
conditions.name: state_elapsed

conditions.doc: Rolls dnp.random, which is seeded per world and replays identically. The ONLY condition that is not a pure read; it is here rather than in `lua` because refire, wander and pain all want it and none of them should have to compile a chunk.
conditions.name: chance

conditions.doc: The named var holds an absolute tick; true once it has passed. A deadline rather than a counter, so a mob nobody is near is not paying to tick one down.
conditions.name: cooldown_ready

args.doc: Ticks. Default 1 -- this tick.
args.name: within

conditions.doc: Something damaged it recently. The pain-state edge.
conditions.name: was_hurt

args.doc: Only this kind. Absent means any mob at all.
args.name: mob

args.doc: Default true. False finds corpses, which is what a resurrector wants to look for before it commits to the animation.
args.name: alive

conditions.doc: Another mob is within reach. Itself never counts.
conditions.name: mob_within

args.doc: Only this catalogue record. Absent means any prop.
args.name: prop

conditions.doc: A prop is within reach -- a barrel to shoot, a totem to guard, a key somebody dropped. Props are not mobs and have no graph; this is how a brain notices the furniture.
conditions.name: prop_within

conditions.doc: At least this many mobs of that kind are within reach. A monster that only charges in a group, or one that panics alone.
conditions.name: count_within

conditions.doc: What it is currently hunting. Since `target_nearest` can point a mob at something that is not a player, a graph that cares has to be able to ask.
conditions.name: target_is

conditions.doc: What hurt it was another mob, not a player. The infighting edge.
conditions.name: hurt_by_mob

args.doc: An expression over `mob`, returning truthy.
args.name: code

args.doc: A Lua function taking `mob`. Needs no compiler at run time, so it works under Trust::Strict where `code` does not.
args.name: fn

conditions.doc: The escape hatch. Anything the vocabulary cannot say.
conditions.name: lua

missile_fields.doc: Which catalogue record this missile is drawn from, and whose radius it hits with. Defaults to the missile's own name, as a mob's does.
missile_fields.name: prop

missile_fields.doc: What it collides with, as a radius. Absent means the `prop`'s own radius from assets/props.txt, which is usually right -- a missile that hits with a different size than it is drawn is a missile players learn to distrust.
missile_fields.name: radius

missile_fields.doc: How far above the shooter's feet it appears. Doom launches from mid-body; a missile born at ankle height clips the first step it crosses.
missile_fields.name: z_offset

missile_fields.doc: Zero for a Doom fireball, which flies flat. Nonzero for a grenade.
missile_fields.name: gravity

missile_fields.doc: Ticks before it expires on its own. A missile with no ceiling on its life leaks a prop slot per shot.
missile_fields.name: life

missile_fields.doc:
Degrees per tick it may turn towards its target. A revenant's missile. Absent means it flies straight.
An INT, not an fx: angles here are brad -- a turn is 2^32 -- and brad is a plain Lua number, because 2^32 is exact in a double. Declaring it `fx` made it an fx userdata that then met plain arithmetic and raised.
missile_fields.name: homing

missile_fields.doc: Runs when it reaches something, with the thing it reached as the target. This is where the damage and the splash go -- so a rocket is a missile whose on_hit is a damage_area, and nothing in the runtime knows what a rocket is.
missile_fields.name: on_hit

mob_fields.doc: Which catalogue record is this mob's BODY. Defaults to the mob's own name, which is what you want: a mob and its body are one thing said in two files, and restating the name in the second one is how they come to disagree. assets/props.txt owns the radius, height, speed, solid flag and the sprites, because the client reads that file too. NOTHING in THIS file crosses the wire: a client that needed a pain chance to draw a monster would be a protocol leak. Name a record here only to make two mobs share one body deliberately.
mob_fields.name: prop

mob_fields.doc: The engine has no notion of health. This is the script's.
mob_fields.name: hp

mob_fields.doc: Which state a freshly spawned mob enters. Defaults to the first state in declaration order.
mob_fields.name: initial

mob_fields.doc: Per-mob counters, by name, with their starting values. Each mob gets its own copy at spawn. This is where a refire count, a spawn budget or a grudge lives.
mob_fields.name: vars

mob_fields.doc: How far this mob notices a target at all. A cheap distance gate checked before anything expensive -- `target_visible` casts a ray, and a ray for every monster on a Doom level every tick is the cost this exists to avoid.
mob_fields.name: sight

mob_fields.doc: 0-255, rolled when the mob is hurt: the chance it flinches at all. Doom's number, because it is a good one -- a monster that ALWAYS flinches can be stun-locked, and one that never does gives no feedback that a hit landed.
mob_fields.name: pain_chance

mob_fields.doc: Turns per second the body may rotate. The engine's default is 4, which is a quarter of a second to come ninety degrees -- and a monster fires along the direction its BODY is pointing, not the one it is aiming at, so a body that lags its target wastes shots into the nearest wall. In a corridor a few degrees off is a wall a metre away, which is what a tracer that renders as a stub is showing you.
mob_fields.name: turn_speed

mob_fields.doc:
How much MORE than a step this mob can gain by hopping. Absent or zero is design §3.2.2's rule -- enemies do not jump -- and routes exactly as it always did.
It is a ROUTING capability and a promise: the nav graph will plan through rises up to this, and the runtime then presses jump where the route says to. Setting it higher than the mob's `jump_impulse` can actually reach gives routes it cannot walk, and the symptom is a monster pressed into a ledge forever.
mob_fields.name: jump_height

mob_fields.doc: Sets gravity_scale to zero at spawn and lets `move` drive Z. Costs no engine support: gravity_scale is a replicated parameter, so a flying monster is flying on every client without a word of it crossing the wire.
mob_fields.name: flying

mob_fields.doc: For a flyer: how far above its target's feet it tries to sit.
mob_fields.name: hover_z

mob_fields.doc: Whether being hurt by another mob makes that mob the target. Doom's monsters do this and it is most of what makes a crowded room interesting.
mob_fields.name: infighting

mob_fields.doc: Whether the body stays after the death state's sequence ends. Corpses are capped and recycled oldest-first by the runtime.
mob_fields.name: corpse

state_fields.doc: The animation state number the client already understands -- the `state <n>` on a sprite line in assets/props.txt. The server declares it and the client owns the timing (design §4), so this is a number, not a frame list.
state_fields.name: anim

state_fields.doc: How the body is driven while in this state. `free` means the state's own actions drive it and the runtime keeps its hands off -- what a scripted leap or a custom controller wants.
state_fields.name: move

state_fields.doc: Where it looks. Separate from `move` because a monster backing away from you while still facing you is a different thing from one turning its back, and Doom's flee does the first.
state_fields.name: face

state_fields.doc: How long the state lasts. Absent means until a transition fires -- which is what `chase` wants and what an attack does not.
state_fields.name: ticks

state_fields.doc: Where it goes when `ticks` runs out. Absent with `ticks` set is a state that ends and stays, which the loader refuses.
state_fields.name: next

state_fields.doc: Ordered {at = <ticks after entry>, ...action}. `at` is relative to entering the state and is a DEADLINE, not a countdown: a mob nobody is near costs nothing between its own decisions.
state_fields.name: sequence

state_fields.doc: Ordered { to = <state>, when = {conditions} }. FIRST MATCH WINS, and order is the priority -- there is no scoring and no backtracking, because a graph whose behaviour depends on a weighting nobody can see is not one an editor can show you.
state_fields.name: transitions

state_fields.doc: Whether pain and death may cut this state short. Death ignores it; nothing interrupts dying.
state_fields.name: interruptible

state_fields.doc: Collision while in this state. A corpse sets it false, which is why you can walk over one.
state_fields.name: solid
